title: Rebirth — Jody Chan
body: This event was initially on Sunday, August 18th however due to extreme weather conditions on the 17th and 18th, it has been rescheduled for safety reasons to Sunday, August 25, 2024 from 2:00 pm to 4:00 pm. We’re sorry for any inconvenience!

Join us for the final session of Tender Possibilities' 2024 Summer Series at Guild Park! Together, we’ll explore poems that consider the cyclical nature of rebirth: how shedding and renewal are integral parts of life. Poems that invite us to challenge the finality of death and explore rebirth as transformation—an emotional, physical journey and healing force.
This session will be facilitated by featured poet Jody Chan and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Jody Chan is a poet, care worker, and community organizer based in Toronto/Tkaronto. They are the author of two books of poetry, sick (Black Lawrence Press) and impact statement (Brick Books), a member of Daybreak Poets Collective, co-host of the new podcast Poet Talk, and an editorial board member of Midnight Sun Magazine.

Special shoutout to Scarborough Arts for their ongoing support and funding part of this session.

title: Nature — Amy Ching-Yan Lam
body: “There are no solitary beings. The whole planet is one giant, living, breathing cell, with all its working parts linked in symbiosis. . . . We do not exist independently." —Thích Nhất Hạnh

Join us for a special session of Tender Possibilities as we explore the theme of nature. We will reflect on water as a symbol of flow, source, and duality—representing both strength and fragility, determination and vulnerability. Together, we will confront the realities of an era where the survival of our planet is uncertain.

Departing from traditional forms, we will examine how poetry can address environmental crises and political instabilities. Poetry that investigates the affective, sensory, and historical contours of the environment. Poems that focus on specific experiences amidst climate collapse and late capitalism. We aim to use poetry as a tool to reconnect with the Earth and explore our responsibilities to it.
This session will be facilitated by featured poet Amy Ching-Yan Lam and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Amy Ching-Yan Lam is an artist and writer. Her first book of poetry, Baby Book (2023, Brick Books) was a finalist for the 2023 Governor General’s Literary Awards in Poetry. Other publications include Looty Goes to Heaven (2022, Eastside Projects) and Property Journal (forthcoming 2024, Book Works). From 2006 to 2020 she was part of the duo Life of a Craphead. She lives in Tkaronto/Toronto, and was born in Hong Kong.

title: Resistance — Nasim Asgari
body: When we speak of resistance, it is crucial to understand both what and why we are resisting. Through curated poems, this session is dedicated to exploring the language of rebellion, resistance, and love for community—a language that cements our bonds and commitments to a shared political ethic. Resistance insists on new possibilities of becoming.

Poetry can resist in two ways—on the level of political consciousness and on the level of form. What if poetry is a kind of resistance itself—anti-rhetorical, a state anterior to politics, the ground of opening into the possible?
This session will be facilitated by featured poet Nasim Asgari and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Tehran-born, Tkaronto-based Nasim Asgari is a dreamer, thinker, seeker and student of the truth. She is a multidisciplinary artist– songwriting, poetry, media arts and performance at the core of her practice. Writing from the age of 9 and performing since 12, she has cultivated a voice and words to relay the truth and bring attention to who and what is systematically undermined and dismissed. Nasim has performed, published, and facilitated workshops and events and contributed internationally to art exhibitions, movies, poetry slams, and TV shows. She is currently completing her MFA in Creative Writing at the University of British Columbia, exploring textiles, writing music, and completing her second poetry collection.

title: Movement — Elizabeth Mudenyo
body: "To perceive is to be the movement, not the object." - Etel Adnan, Journey to Mount Tamalpais

This session of Tender Possibilities will explore narratives of movement, displacement, migration, and return. Movement defines our stories. Migration embodies both the deeply human desire to move and the political conditions that often necessitate leaving one’s home. Our bodies themselves are dynamic vessels of movement, from the rhythmic cycles of breath and heartbeat to the profound transformations we undergo throughout our lives. By examining the intersections of life, community, place, and bodies, our aim is to uncover how movement and migration define and reshape our understanding of the world.
Facilitation by featured poet Elizabeth Mudenyo and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Elizabeth Mudenyo is a Scarborough-based poet, community-engaged artist and arts manager. Elizabeth is a fellow of The Watering Hole and the Poetry Incubator, and a participant of the Hurston/Wright Poetry Weekend with Danez Smith and Diaspora Dialogues Short Form Mentorship with Olive Senior. Her work has appeared in Write Magazine, Arc Magazine, The Ex-Puritan, Canthius, CV2, and elsewhere. Her poetry chapbook, With Both Hands, was published through Anstruther Press. She is a graduate of the MFA in Creative Writing from the University of Guelph.

title: Memory — Hoa Nguyen
body: "Memory isn't something that blooms but something that bleeds internally." — Victoria Chang.

This session of Tender Possibilities invites us to reflect on how memory shapes our identities and narratives. Memory preserves a close emotional distance to life. Memory is who we are. It is the story we tell ourselves about where we come from and how we got to be here now. We will explore poems that bridge personal recollections and communal histories, challenging us to critically consider the role of memory in our lives and social environments. We’ll see how a single poem, rooted in the writer’s memory, can unlock completely different memories in the minds of readers, creating a shared yet unique experience for each participant.
The second session of our summer series will be facilitated by featured poet, Hoa Nguyen and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Born in the lower Mekong Delta and raised in the Washington DC area, Hoa Nguyen is a poet and educator teaching writing and poetics at Toronto Metropolitan University. Her books include Red Juice, the Griffin Prize-nominated Violet Energy Ingots, and A Thousand Times You Lose Your Treasure, a finalist for the National Book Award and the General Governor’s Literary Award. She’s the 2024 recipient of the C.D. Wright Award in Poetry from the Foundation of Contemporary Art, an Aquarius, and a Fire Horse.

title: Origin with Zoe Imani Sharpe
body: Join us for the first session of Tender Possibilities’ 2024 Summer Series, where we'll explore the theme of Origin. Through curated poems, we'll reflect on beginnings, roots, and the foundational moments that shape our identity and existence. Origin calls to mind ancestral narratives, and the cultural legacies that inform our understanding of ourselves and the world. Origin is a continuous dialogue with the past and an acknowledgment of the influences that have brought us to the present.
This session will be facilitated by featured poet Zoe Imani Sharpe and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Zoe Imani Sharpe is a poet, editor, teacher and workshop-maker. Her writing embraces desire and intuition, the sensuality of aesthetics, lineage, loss and mourning, women’s labour and practices of vitality. Her recent collaborations include an exploration of “life writing” called Bout That Life (Gallery TPW), a workshop gathering disparate citational materials; WhAt She SAid: Promiscuous References & Disobedient Care (Contingencies of Care, OCADU), and the intersubjective text Power, Baby! (with Claire Freeman-Fawcett). She was the 2023 Poet-In-Residence at Gallery TPW. You can find her recent work in YYZ Artists’ Outlet, carteblanche and Best Canadian Poetry 2021.
